The rule compares a yield with an unspecified endpoint, and here the endpoint is after the neck.

the sheet publishes 145 MPa at break, a 7.7 GPa modulus and 1.5% elongation. A short-fibre composite's modulus is measured over the first quarter of a per cent of strain and its curve stiffens after that, so the break strain is below stress over modulus. All three are the sheet's own.

the sheet publishes a Z strength, a Z modulus and a Z elongation whose ratio does not close. A printed part fails at its layer boundary before the bulk reaches that strain, and all three are the sheet's own.

the sheet prints 70 kg-cm/cm, which is 686 J/m. Notched Izod of 600 to 900 J/m is ordinary for polycarbonate: it is the toughest of the amorphous engineering polymers, and the window's 600 is drawn from a database that held no PC value.
the sheet prints "Notched Izod Impact Strength 6 J/m D 256" for PLA Magic SILK. A silk PLA is brittle and 6 J/m is what its sheet publishes.

the sheet prints a tensile strength at yield of 57.5 MPa and at break of 14.2 MPa for THE FILAMENT PLA CF. A short-fibre composite that has yielded carries little at the point of separation; both numbers are the sheet's own.
the sheet prints "Notched Izod Impact Strength 8.3 J/m ISO 180" for FlameGuard PLA. A flame-retardant load embrittles a PLA further, and 8.3 J/m is the sheet's own number.

the sheet prints "Elongation at Break 400% ISO D882" for rPETG. ASTM D882 is a thin-film test and a film stretches far more than a printed bar; the standard the sheet names is recorded with the value.
